By one month, the estimate of 73.76 edges a bit higher still, incorporating the idea that over longer horizons, any modest bullish bias compounds, though the effect remains small in absolute terms.

The confidence interval widths expand considerably as the horizon lengthens, which is a standard feature of forecasting under uncertainty. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly 71.2 to 75.3 reflects typical daily volatility — markets can move a few percent in a day, but rarely more than that without a major shock. On the downside, a credit event, a sharp commodity price move, or a liquidity crunch in financial markets could send prices below the lower bound.
